one_month_reasoning: AMD has not announced its Q3 date; Nov 3 is an aggregator estimate (MarketBeat) and in 2 of the last 5 years (Oct 26 2021, Oct 29 2024) Q3 printed before Oct 30, so I put ~25-30% on the print (and Q4 guide, first Helios revenue) landing inside the window. Also in-window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC after the Sep-16 hike, and late-October hyperscaler Q3 reports and 2027 capex guides. Direction of these is unknown; the stock ran ~32% into late September and pulled back to $604, so reversal vs momentum roughly cancel, with a slight skeptic tilt from valuation downgrades and ongoing CEO 10b5-1 sales. Net: near-symmetric distribution centred just under spot (~$600) with sigma ~20% (72%/3.5), tails widened ~0.5pp versus round 1 for the possible in-window earnings event.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) P/E on NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$19.7 (0.25 x $15.58 FY27 + 0.75 x $21 FY28) x 29x, less 4.5% dilution, plus ~$6/share net cash = ~$551 (60%), and (b) FY2028 EPS $21 x 30x discounted one year at 10%, less 4.5% dilution and ~$3/share expected cost of customer-financing commitments, plus net cash = ~$550 (40%). Blended ~$550, ~9% below spot.

methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 $19.7 x 29x = $571; x (1-4.5%) dilution = $545; + ~$6/share net cash = ~$551

AMD's August notes priced at 4.6-5.5% and the Fed is hiking; ~10% cost of equity for a high-beta (72% vol) semi.

inputs_detail.value: $4.1B lease guarantees (up to 15 yrs), $5.0B investment commitments through FY2028, $9.5B new long-term data-center leases, $30.3B purchase commitments
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q (June 27 plus subsequent events). Expected cost set at ~$5B (~$3/share): ~10% expected loss on guarantees plus a ~50% haircut on the value of the $5B equity-style investments into customers/partners; the purchase commitments are a bear-case inventory risk, not a base-case cost.

bear.story: Helios ramp is slower than the 'significant Q4 step-up, further Q1'27 step-up' path (rack integration complexity, customers' power/financing constraints), and/or 2027 AI capex digests; FY27 EPS ~$12-13 vs $15.58; AMD's customer-financing stack ($4.1B lease guarantees, $5B investment commitments, $9.5B leases, $30.3B purchase commitments, penny warrants) is read as vendor financing of weak organic demand, and the multiple compresses to ~25x forward. ~$340.

base.story: Q3 near the $13B guide, Helios shipments step up in Q4 and 1H27 as guided, FY27 EPS ~$15-15.6 and FY28 path ~$21; strong growth offset by de-rating from ~42x NTM to ~29-30x plus ~4.5% dilution, so the stock is roughly flat.

bull.story: OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic/Oracle deployments scale on schedule, data-center revenue more than doubles in 2027 as guided, estimates keep rising (FY27 consensus already +18% in 90 days), FY28 path toward $26-28, and the market keeps ~33-35x forward.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$400 (-34%, ~26x FY27 consensus and ~19x a $21 FY28 path, below the August 2026 breakout base) would most likely mean the guided 2027 data-center doubling is broken: a genuine Helios/MI450 ramp shortfall beyond Q1'27 (not the denied Feb-2026 report), a cut to OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic first-GW commitments, a partner default calling AMD's lease guarantees, or a hyperscaler 2027 capex reset.

reasoning: Round 2 corrections, from the supervisor and checked in the 10-Q: (1) the Feb-2026 Helios slip-to-Q2-2027 report was denied and superseded by the Aug-4 call ('in production, initial shipments later this quarter, ramp through Q4 and into 2027'); a Sep-2026 search found shipments starting and no newer delay report, so I dropped the $14 EPS leg; (2) net cash is ~$9.9B (cash+ST $13.1B vs $3.25B debt; I had added the August notes' debt without their cash); (3) the current multiple is ~39x FY27 / ~42x NTM, not '80x forward'; (4) World Labs adds ~13.6M shares. The skeptic leg is rebuilt on current evidence: the 10-Q shows AMD increasingly financing its customers ($4.1B lease guarantees 'may be issued in exchange for warrants', $5.0B investment commitments through FY28 and $9.5B of new long-term data-center leases entered after quarter-end, $30.3B purchase commitments, inventory $8.5B, receivables $7.3B), which with the penny warrants means reported margins overstate economic margins and demand is partly vendor-financed. I price that as a small per-share cost and as bear-case probability, not as a base EPS haircut. I also switched from FY28 EPS to a proper NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ($19.7), which offsets the upward corrections, so fair value stays ~$550 (29-30x, a skeptic's view that a ~30% de-rating is likely; the supervisor's $580 uses 30x and I disagree only on that one turn of multiple plus the financing cost). Distribution: scenario mean ~$610, median ~$580, lognormal sigma ~0.5 with a fat left tail; P(>=spot) raised from 45.5% to 47% and the centre of the ladder up ~1-1.5pp because the stale delay risk is removed. No short-seller report or securities class action found. Research in round 2 was tight: one 10-Q fetch and three searches.
